```{r}
UniversalBank<-read.csv("UniversalBank (1).csv")
dim(UniversalBank)
```


```{r}
library(reshape2)
library(e1071)
```

# data prep

```{r}
Bank <- data.frame(Loan = factor(UniversalBank$Personal.Loan),
Online = factor(UniversalBank$Online),
Creditcard = factor(UniversalBank$CreditCard))
set.seed(1)

idx <-sample(nrow(Bank), .6 * nrow(Bank))
train <- Bank[idx, ]
valid <-Bank[-idx, ]

nrow(train)
nrow(valid)
table(train$Loan)
```
# pivot table
```{r}
train$count <- 1
long <- melt(train, id.vars = c( "Creditcard", "Loan", "Online"), measure.vars  ="count")
pivot <- dcast(long, Creditcard + Loan ~ Online, fun.aggregate = sum)
pivot

```

# P(loan= 1 | creditcard = 1, Online=1) pivot tables

```{r}
t3 <- xtabs(~Creditcard +Loan + Online, data= train)
t3

p_8 <- t3["1","1", "1"]/(t3["1","1", "1"] + t3["1","0", "1"])
p_8
```

#about 9.1% of customers accept these loans
#2 pivot table
```{r}
tabonline<- xtabs(~Loan + Online, data= train)
tab_ccc<- xtabs(~Loan +Creditcard,  data=train)

tabonline
tab_ccc
```
# Quantites
```{r}
n1<- sum(train$Loan == "1")
m0 <-sum(train$Loan == "0")
pcc <- tab_ccc["1", "1"] / n1
ponline <-tabonline["1", "1"] / n1
p1 <-n1 / nrow(train)
p_cc <-tab_ccc["0", "1"] /m0
pponline <-tabonline["0","1"] /m0
p <- m0 / nrow(train)

data.frame(quantity= c("P(CC=1|Loan=1)", "P(Online=1|Loan=1)", "P(Loan=1)",
                        "P(CC=1|Loan=0)", "P(Online=1|Loan=0)", "P(Loan=0)"),
         value = round(c(pcc,ponline,p1,p_cc,pponline,p), 4))
```

```{r}
num<- pcc * ponline * p1
den <- num + p_cc * pponline * p
p_Z <- num /den
p_Z
```
# .09055758
```{r}
newB<-naiveBayes(Loan ~ Online + Creditcard, data= train)
newB
predict(newB,
        newdata = data.frame(Online = factor("1", levels = c("0", "1")),
        Creditcard =factor("1", levels = c("0", "1"))),
        type ="raw")
```
# pivot table had a 9.1% and naive had a .09055.Meaning they are alomost identical and those the pivot table is an exaclty taken from all the data wear as the naive Bayes is a n approximation using 2 data sets
